newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy opposition to hold anti-budget rally Nov 9.
newsitem.headline: Italy opposition to hold anti-budget rally Nov 9.

text.p: Italy's opposition centre-right Freedom Alliance plans to hold a demonstration in Rome on November 9 to protest against the government's 1997 budget, political sources said on Wednesday.
The sources said the date for the demonstration was decided at a meeting of party leaders.

Pierferdinando Casini, leader of the centrist CCD party in former Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi's Freedom Alliance, said the government risked sparking a "revolution" unless it scrapped plans to increase property taxes,
"The government must remove the house tax by tomorrow afternoon unless they want a revolution," Casini told reporters.
"There are also other points that are unacceptable...this is a budget totally based on taxes," he added.

The budget, which was approved by Prime Minister Romano Prodi's cabinet last week and is due to be officially presented to parliament on Thursday, aims to cut 62.5 trillion lire off next year's projected deficit.

Among measures included in the budget is a five percent increase in taxes on house and land ownership as well as a five percent increase in the valuations local authorities can base their property taxes on.

The plan has drawn fire from across the political spectrum with the largest party in the government coalition, the Democratic Party of the Left (PDS), as well as the unions demanding alternative proposals.
The Freedom Alliance is due to present its "counter-budget" on Thursday.
